text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds held on to their gains in late trade, underpinned by continued strength in U.S. Treasury prices and a favourable technical outlook. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.55, up 0.36 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts tumbled into the close and underperformed other major bond markets as worries grew about the outlook for interest rates. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-12/32, down 12/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and PIBOR futures finished higher in moderate volume in a market again turned optimistic which could quickly test its contract high of 126.80. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.46, up 0.46 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures rose steadily throughout the day, helped by the firmer trend on other world bond markets, especially U.S. Treasuries, and encouraging words from the government on progress towards ERM and EMU membership. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 122.95, up 0.84 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities stood near session highs after midday, holding on to the majority their overseas gains in quiet trade. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-16/32, up 12/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.77 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond futures contract ended near the day's high as day traders quickly moved to cover short positions after it failed to crack support at 122.40. In after-hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.93, up 0.09 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market got off to a slow start but saw two sizeable dollar bonds in the both the fixed- and the floating-rate sectors. Triple-A rated Suedwestdeutsche LB Capital Markets launched a larger-than-expected $750 million five-year bond which was priced to yield 14 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes and pay a 6.375 percent coupon. Also in dollars, the National Australia Bank set a $500 million two-year FRN at 10 b.p. through three-month LIBOR. In the lira sector, DSL Bank added 100 billion lire to its 10-year 8.0 percent bond.
